title: Los Aretes de Jojutla, MEXI STORIES
comment: aretes-jojutla (MEXI): corredor de la casa grande de una hacienda arrocera en Jojutla, Morelos, a media mañana. Caras comunes, no famosas; los tres se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.LEONARDA_MONTOYA: Mexican woman, feared matriarch of a rice hacienda, 67 years old, tanned skin, grey-streaked black hair in a thick braided crown around her head, hard dark eyes, deep lines around the mouth, a dark-green long-sleeve dress with a black shawl over her shoulders, a wide leather belt, a small silver cross necklace, her hands empty.
chars.ISADORA_MONTOYA: Mexican woman, the matriarch's eldest daughter, 28 years old, light-brown skin, long wavy black hair loose over one shoulder, soft brown eyes, a white linen blouse with a square neckline, a long terracotta skirt, a pair of distinctive long silver filigree drop earrings shaped like teardrops, her hands empty.
chars.ABEL_CORTES: Mexican man, new hacienda worker looking for a job, 33 years old, dark-brown skin, short black hair, a thin black mustache, strong jaw, serious dark eyes, a faded denim work shirt with rolled sleeves over a white t-shirt, jeans, work boots, a straw cowboy hat in his hand, his hands otherwise empty.

locs.LOC_HACIENDAJOJUTLA: Wide corridor of the main house of an old rice hacienda in Jojutla, Morelos, in the bright mid-morning: thick ochre stone arches, red clay tile floor, potted ferns and bougainvillea, a wooden bench, and beyond the arches green rice fields and tall palm trees under a hot blue sky, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
